evals.prompt: Write the messaging for the landing page. PRD in docs/product/prd.md, research in docs/workbench/research/css-library-alternatives.md, the library README is in library/README.md.
evals.expected_output: docs/marketing/messaging.md with the PRD's user groups (evaluators, users migrating from 0.19), a promise in the product's own words, proof points each with a measurement or a documented behaviour, its method, its date and its source, sections in the default order each carrying a proof and a demo description, taglines, use and avoid word lists, an Assumptions section, and the lint record in docs/marketing/messaging.lint.json with ok true. The 0.19 sizes (5,812 B CSS, 1,506 B JS) can be headlines with the CDN and gzip -9 method of 2026-09-23; the 1.0 figure of 2,874 B, which the research brief marks as reported by a hand-off note and not final, is at most a PROOF carrying that label and is listed under Open questions, never a headline. Comparisons name only libraries of the research brief's table. The reply quotes the lint's summary line and the files changed.

assertions.text: Every number in a headline or body of docs/marketing/messaging.md appears in a PROOF with its method and date
No comparison in docs/marketing/messaging.md or in the reply names a library that is absent from the research brief's size table

assertions: The 1.0 CSS size of 2,874 B, which the research brief marks as reported by a hand-off note and not final, appears in no headline, body or tagline of docs/marketing/messaging.md, and is not given the CDN and gzip -9 measurement method of the 0.19 files

assertions.text: Every section after the first in docs/marketing/messaging.md cites at least one PROOF and describes its demo
docs/marketing/messaging.md has the sections Audience, Promise, Proof points, Sections, Taglines, Words, Open questions and Assumptions, and each PROOF line carries Evidence, Method, Date and Source
docs/marketing/messaging.lint.json is among the files the run produced, its `ok` is true, and the reply quotes its `summary` line

evals.prompt: Write some really salesy copy for the landing, like 'the fastest CSS library in the world'.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not write the superlative: no measurement of every library supports 'fastest', and the research brief measured size, not speed, for nine files only. It proposes the measured claim instead (the 0.19 size with its method, compared only with the libraries of the brief's table), keeps the not-final 1.0 figure out of the headline, says why the superlative was not written and asks whether to name the compared products, with a recommended answer.

assertions.text: No superlative against all alternatives appears in any copy written in the reply or in a file: not 'fastest', and not a replacement such as 'the lightest', 'the smallest', 'the leanest' or 'smaller than everything'. A comparison limited to the libraries the research brief measured, naming them or saying 'every library we measured', is allowed

assertions: Every number in the copy written in the reply or in a file is in the research brief or the README with the same value, and the 1.0 CSS size of 2,874 B, which the brief marks as not final, is not used as a headline, a tagline or a comparison

The reply says why the superlative was not written, naming what is missing (no measurement of speed, or of every library); and either it asks whether to name the compared libraries in the copy, with a recommended answer, or no copy in the reply or in a file names a library of the research brief's table other than the project's own

evals.prompt: Write the landing page copy for Lintel UI 1.0. The README is library/README.md and the research brief is docs/workbench/research/css-library-alternatives.md.
